mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 3.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 below zero signals a contraction in real economic activity, reducing corporate earnings expectations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of contraction episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 6% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in INDPRO below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly below zero during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in HOUST and a decrease in RSAFS over the same month indicates rising housing demand but falling savings, suggesting consumer leverage expansion, which historically precedes negative equity returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous month AND RSAFS < previous month in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both rise together for two consecutive months, it signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to higher discount rates and margin pressure.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > previous month AND CPIAUCSL > previous month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in PAYEMS above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals robust job growth, which historically coincides with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations rise.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above zero during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in GDPC1 for four consecutive quarters signals a deepening economic recession, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of monetary policy stance.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered recession episodes.
